rounds.text: TPI India Ltd is significantly under-appreciated by the market, trading at a price of ₹ 17.4 with a discounted cash flow valuation showing a strong intrinsic value of ₹ 24 per share, offering a substantial margin of safety of 26.2% [E2, E35, E36]. The company exhibits extraordinary operational efficiency, boasting a phenomenal ROCE of 129.0% and an ROA of 19.75%, both vastly outperforming sector benchmarks [E8, E10, E12]. Profitability is compounding aggressively, highlighted by a staggering 592% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months and a 25% compounded profit growth over five years [E18, E20]. This financial strength is backed by pristine cash generation, with operating cash flow reaching ₹ 2.83 Cr and a healthy cash conversion ratio of 1.14x, ensuring profits are fully realized in cash while borrowings simultaneously decreased to ₹ 15.14 Cr [E26, E27, E30]. Operational margins are expanding rapidly, with quarterly operating margins surging to 22% in Mar 2026—a 12 percentage point increase year-over-year alongside an increasing multi-quarter trend [E23, E25]. Furthermore, technical momentum supports the fundamental turnaround, as the stock price trades comfortably above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E40], while a rules-based screen awards the company a solid BUY score of 83 out of 100 [E51]. Conceded: promoter holding has dropped significantly by 34.80 percentage points down to 58.71% [E32], compounded profit growth over 3 years stands at -46% [E19], and annualized volatility is high at 585.4% [E44].

Conceded: the discounted cash flow model suggests a value of ₹ 24 per share [E35]. However, the bull's narrative of continuous compounding glosses over severe fundamental instability, such as a 3-year compounded profit growth of -46% [E19] and a 10-year compounded sales growth of dead-flat 0% [E13]. The boasted operating margins are flagged by Screener as inconsistent over the last 3 years [E24], and debtor days have stretched from 35.4 to 46.8 days [E49], raising questions about the quality of those surging top-line numbers. Furthermore, the extreme annualised volatility of 585.4% [E44] and a devastating historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -99.6% [E43] mean the technical momentum and moving averages cited by the bull [E40] offer little comfort against structural volatility. Most alarmingly, insiders are heavily exiting, with promoter holding collapsing by 34.80 percentage points down to 58.71% [E32]. Finally, the stock trades at an expensive EV/EBITDA of 20.78x against a sector benchmark of just 8.98x [E11], alongside a negative ROE of -21.3% [E9] that completely contradicts the picture of pristine health painted by the bull.
